page: Vultr vbm-6c-32gb is a dedicated bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal SSD family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 2286G processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled, supported by 32.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 2.67 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a 1920 GB local SSD, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching 35.51 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 13.91 GB/sec, placing both in the top 25% tier. The PassMark memory score is highly competitive, ranking in the top 10% tier at 3453.69. However, memory bandwidth for large, potentially uncached blocks shows limitations, with read-only large block speeds at 32.51 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 14.71 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, while the server handles small-model LLM inference adequately, performance drops significantly on medium 7B models, yielding a weak 7.38 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated bare metal allocation eliminates virtualization overhead, offering predictable execution for compute-bound tasks. The combination of high-frequency CPU cores and a substantial 1920 GB local SSD makes this server suitable for database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose workloads that require dedicated hardware without the need for GPU acceleration.
